delve deep into the essentials of Tamil, all her unique features parade into our minds. The very word ‘Tamil’ itself is mellifluous, since it is a synonym for sweetness.

Jeevaka Chinthamani rightly states ‘தமிழ் தழீஇய சாயலவர்’ (Tamil is beauty / elegance personified). The very word ‘Tamil’ is imbibed with consonants hard, soft and medium. Mahakavi Bharathi, a polyglot, sings in praise of Tamil: -

" For sweetness Tamil is unexampled

Of all the tongues that I have sampled”

Manimekalai, Kambaramayanam and Thiruvaimozhi also extol the sweetness of Tamil. Exclusively in Tamil Nadu, one can find original names such as Tamil Selvan, Tamilarasi. When they develop their affinity to Tamil the original names become causatives.

Varadarasan differs from this view stating, “Foreigners often mispronounce the word ‘Tamil’ and hence it took the derivative form ‘Dravidam’”. ADI DRAVIDAR AND TRIBAL WELFARE DEPARTMENT

3.4.1 Payment of scholarship to ineligible students

Non-adherence to Government’s orders by the Director of Adi Dravidar Welfare and District Adi Dravidar and Tribal Welfare Officers, and lack of clarity in the order had resulted in an inadmissible expenditure of ` 1.81 crore towards sanction of Higher Education Special Scholarship to ineligible students.

In 1971-72, the Government of Tamil Nadu (GoTN) launched a loan cum scholarship scheme for Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe (SC/ST) students pursuing higher studies as hostellers. The scheme underwent modifications in 1996-97, 2002-03 and 2011-12. The modified ‘Higher Education Special Scholarship’ (HESS) scheme envisaged a scholarship of ` 7,500 and ` 8,000 per annum to eligible students28 studying in undergraduate and post graduate/professional courses respectively. At the state level, HESS is implemented by the Director of Adi Dravidar Welfare (DADW) and at the district level, the District Adi Dravidar and Tribal Welfare Officers (DADWO) implement the scheme.

Consequent on launching (2013-14) of the centrally sponsored ‘Post Matric Scholarship scheme’ (PMSS) in the current form, GoTN decided (March 2017) to review the need for continuation of HESS as both the schemes offered similar benefits resulting in duplication and increased expenditure. Based on the review, while issuing orders (March 2018) for continuation of HESS for the academic year 2017-18, GoTN restricted the grant of new HESS only to students of Government and Government aided institutions, staying in hostels of the institution or in hostels approved by the institution. The DADW, while allocating scheme funds to DADWOs during 2017-20, also reiterated the above condition for grant of HESS.
